summary: AI Assistant Pass 5 validation. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration141_assistant_pass5.py — 12/12 tests pass covering find_customer routing, attach_note_to_customer + commit-note-to-customer (200/400/404), the full reminder lifecycle (commit-reminder → nudges surfaces it → dismiss-reminder removes it), 404 on bad reminder_id, and regression for all 5 prior tools (navigate / create_task / create_appointment / send_quote_followup_bulk / query_shop_metric). Regression suite test_fees_and_owner_connect.py still 10/10. Frontend wiring confirmed via source inspection: AIAssistant.js has ProposedActionPill cases for both new action_types with the exact required data-testids (proposed-action-find-customer + proposed-action-attach-note plus *-confirm variants), and AssistantNudgesWidget.js has KIND_ICON.reminder=Bell, KIND_COLOR.reminder yellow theme, handleAction's reminder branch posts {reminder_id} to /api/ai/assistant/dismiss-reminder and removes the row from setNudges state.
action_items: Optional polish (not blocking): the natural-language phrase 'remind me to X in 1 minute' was classified by the assistant as set_reminder but came back status='needs_clarification' — the in-N-minutes parsing path may want a tweak. Workaround in test: seed reminders directly via POST /api/ai/assistant/commit-reminder which works perfectly.

Optional polish: AssistantNudgesWidget reminder row's 'Mark done' button has no explicit data-testid — adding data-testid='nudge-mark-done-{reminder_id}' would make UI automation more deterministic, especially when the Confirm-AI-credit-usage modal interferes with downstream clicks.
critical_code_review_comments: assistant_tools.py commit-note-to-customer correctly enforces tenant isolation in both the find query and the update — 404 vs 400 split is right (400 for missing payload fields, 404 for cross-tenant or unknown id). Good.

Note appending uses simple string concat with '\n\n' separator — if a customer accumulates 1000+ notes the field will become huge with no rotation. Consider migrating to an embedded array later (existing /customers PUT notes_append has the same shape so this is consistent for now).
ai.py nudges endpoint: limits to 3 due reminders before the outer slice nudges[:6]. If multiple kinds saturate the list, reminders could be starved. Low priority.

Frontend AssistantNudgesWidget: handleAction dispatches different branches by n.kind. The reminder branch correctly stops after dismiss (returns early) — but it does NOT show a loading spinner on the specific row while POST is in flight (uses page-level setBusy). Minor UX nit.

success_rate.frontend: Wiring verified via code review (data-testids + dismiss-reminder POST handler all present). Live Playwright automation of the chat input was blocked by the Confirm-AI-credit-usage modal that intercepts subsequent fills; not a real bug — see action_items for the optional data-testid suggestion.

seed_data_creation: TEST_pass5_lifecycle_<rand> reminders created via /commit-reminder and immediately dismissed within the same test; one TEST_pass5 note appended to existing Test Customer (d3808427-8b22-430c-ad37-87f1d89c1176) — note persists and accumulates timestamped lines as designed, no cleanup needed (note appends are the feature).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pass 5 backend is solid. If you need to UI-test the AIAssistant chat, first dismiss the 'Confirm AI credit usage' modal (button text 'Continue') OR call POST /api/ai/credit-confirm/preference with show_confirm=false (if such endpoint exists) before each chat send. The frontend uses cookie-based session (httpOnly), so window.localStorage.token will be empty — use credentials:'include' on fetches or do everything through the rendered UI. To seed reminders for the nudges widget, POST /api/ai/assistant/commit-reminder with {text, remind_at: <ISO past>}.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. All 4 new endpoints behave exactly per spec. The single test-harness friction (set_reminder natural-language phrasing returning needs_clarification) is documented as an optional polish item, with a clean workaround via the existing /commit-reminder direct endpoint.
